plumbing.review:
I've finished reading the change against the plan and the surrounding code. Here's the review.

**Bottom line:** The server side does what the plan says and nothing more, and I found no security problems. One bug on the page: right after a post, the headline's "N issues need you" count still includes the issue you just acted on. The plan says it should drop out of that count. The fix is one line.

### 1. Does what the plan says, and nothing more

What matches:
- **act.go (trusted) changes only as the plan allows.** The only additions are `s.took(c, url)` at `internal/dashboard/act.go:430` (Ratify all) and `:502` (single post). Each runs only after GitHub took the post; a refused post returns or breaks first (`:423-428`, `:496-499`).
- **Same rule the factory's reading uses.** `took` decides "gives it what it waits for" with the existing `answered` (`issues.go:327`), the function Lane uses at `issues.go:257`. It rewrites the stage exactly as Lane does (`acted.go:172-174` vs `issues.go:261-263`).
- **The note is left out.** `command` is `TrimSpace(c.Body)` (`acted.go:52`), and the agent's note is only added to what goes to GitHub (`act.go:495`).
- **The five texts** are at `acted.go:74-87`, chosen by the first verb, as `commandText` does.
- **Refuses the same command twice.** `serve` puts the applied issues in `s.issues` (`acted.go:149`), which `post` and `ratifyAll` check against (`act.go:488-491`, `:400-403`).
- **Forgetting works in production too.** `publish` drops a kept command when its URL is among its issue's comments (`acted.go:96-102`, `:124-125`). The listing and `PostComment` both decode `html_url` into `Comment.URL` (`internal/github/github.go:68`, `:187-189`).
- **dashboard.go** publishes through acted.go (`dashboard.go:492`) and loads the last run through it (`:541`).
- **issues.go** adds `Acted` (`issues.go:71-74`).
- **SPEC.md** adds the one sentence the plan asks for. The README only mentions `/act` historically (`README.md:150`), so it's right to leave it alone.
- **Scope.** Every file touched is in the plan's list, and nothing under `decisions/` changed.
- **One small addition:** a kept command only applies while its issue still waits on the same factory post (`acted.go:163`). It's a sensible guard.

**Bug (blocking): the needs-you count isn't redrawn at once.**
- The headline chip "1 issue needs you" (`web/app.js:166-167`, D-0098's count) is drawn only when `changed("now", …)` at `app.js:117` is true. That key covers `now`, `nowBy`, `factory`, `main`, `receipts` and `repos`, but no issues.
- An at-once serve re-marshals the same read with only `issues` changed (`acted.go:138`). So after `/act` reloads (`app.js:1477`, `:1509`), `renderNow` doesn't run.
- Result: the chip still counts the acted issue while Needs you says "Nothing needs you right now" above the acted card (`app.js:1271`).
- It stays that way until a later refresh changes one of those fields. By default that's up to 30 s (`cmd/invariant/main.go:895`), which is the delay #175 is meant to remove. The plan says an acted issue is "left out of the count of what needs you".

Not blocking, but worth knowing:
- **Only three fields change.** `apply` sets `waiting`, `stage` and `acted` (`acted.go:159-178`) and leaves `spans` and `now` alone. Until the refresh:
  - The lane shows the "queued" chip (`app.js:852`) next to an open people segment reading "waiting …" (`app.js:861`), and `peopleSeconds` keeps growing.
  - An idle headline doesn't become "Picking up #N" as it would from the factory's reading (`dashboard.go:1272-1291`).
  
  The plan and tests name only those three fields, so this isn't blocking.
- **Split answers don't show at once.** `took` looks only at the new command (`acted.go:53,60`). The factory's reading counts every command since its post (`issues.go:251-257`). So answering F1 and F2 in separate posts doesn't show at once. The page can't do this (it posts only once every fork is chosen, `app.js:1426`); only the agent's door can.
- **A command can get stuck.** A command is forgotten only when a refresh finds its comment. If the comment never shows up (for example, it's deleted right away), the issue stays acted-on until the factory posts again or the dashboard restarts. Meanwhile `/act` refuses to post it again (`act.go:236-237`). This is the plan's design, and worth a line in the decision that refines D-0093.

### 2. Acceptance tests
- `acted_accept_test.go` is the plan's source, unchanged. Nothing in acted.go depends on the test fixtures (repo, issue numbers, hashes). The texts come from the issue's `Waiting` and the command's verb.
- `TestActDrawsWhatWasPosted` only checks that `.acted` and `.command` appear in app.js. The code really does read them (`app.js:1257`, `:1278-1281`), but the test can't catch drawing bugs like the chip one.
- The last part of `TestTheRefreshThatReadsTheCommentTakesOver` would pass even without forgetting, because of the guard at `acted.go:163`. The code does forget, though (`:96-102`).
- tests.txt shows gofmt, vet, the package tests and all four acceptance tests passing. It doesn't mention `-race`, so I checked the locking by hand:
  - `r.src.comments` is read only in `publish`, which runs on the refresh goroutine that writes it.
  - Locks are always taken `acted.mu` then `mu`, and the handlers release `mu` before calling `took`.

### 3. Checks, network, secrets
- **No check weakened.** `act.check` and `batch.check` are untouched, and the applied view only clears `Waiting`, so it can only make them refuse more.
- **No new network or host access.** `took` and `serve` work only in memory.
- **No secrets.** `acted` carries no email and not the agent's note. `check` limits commands to `/invariant` lines with IDs or hex (`act.go:240-256`), so the public `state.json` gains no free text; the plan asks for it on every page. `actedCard` escapes everything it draws (`app.js:1279-1282`).

### 4. Reads like the code around it
- acted.go matches act.go: a comment block at the top with the issue number, doc comments in the same voice, short verb names, and field comments like `Waiting`'s. The CSS mirrors `.need.failed` (`style.css:640-646` vs `:763-766`).
- Optional nits:
  - `serve` reads like an HTTP handler next to `serveAct` and `serveGzip`.
  - The D-0093 stage rule is now in two places (`acted.go:172-174`, `issues.go:261-263`).
  - A superseded read that fails still shows "can't reach the server" (`app.js:106-107`).

VERDICT: changes needed — the headline's needs-you count must redraw when an at-once reload changes what waits: add the waiting issues to the `"now"` key at `internal/dashboard/web/app.js:117` (e.g. `s.issues.filter((i) => i.open && i.waiting).map(issueKey)`), so an acted issue leaves the count at once, as the plan says.

usage.summary:
Issue #175's plan is built, and every check passes on the final files: gofmt, `go vet`, the dashboard package's tests and all four acceptance tests. It took 2 of the 6 runs.

**What changed**
- **`act.go`** (trusted base): `post` and `ratifyAll` each gained one line that hands every command GitHub took to `s.took`. Nothing else changed.
- **`acted.go`** (new): keeps the last snapshot read and the commands GitHub took. Each command's issue is served waiting on no one and queued, with `acted` set to `command`, `text`, `url` and `at`. Each refresh drops any kept command whose comment URL it has read among its issue's comments, and serves the rest still applied. One lock covers every publish, so a post and a refresh never overwrite each other.
- **`dashboard.go`**: the refresh and the snapshot loaded at startup now both publish through `acted.go`. `issues.go` adds the `acted` field to `Issue`.
- **Page** (`app.js`, `style.css`): after GitHub takes a post, /act reads `/api/state.json` again at once. Needs you shows acted issues after the waiting ones, as cards with the command, its text, when it was posted and a link to the comment, and nothing to post. They aren't counted in what needs you. The public page is unchanged.
- **`SPEC.md`**: the /act bullet now says a command GitHub takes shows at once, on every page, until a read of GitHub finds its comment. It cites only the decisions it already cited.

**Calls the plan didn't settle**
- **Partial answers:** a command is kept only if it alone gives its issue what it waits for. An answer to one of two questions isn't kept. If the second answer is then posted on its own, it shows only after a refresh reads both comments.
- **Stale commands:** a kept command applies only while its issue still waits on the same factory post it answered. If the factory moves on before its comment is read, the old command never overrides the new state.
- **Which text shows:** it follows the command's first line, since that's the one the factory acts on.
- **Saved snapshot:** the copy saved between runs is the served one, with commands applied. A restart before the comment is read won't offer the same command again.
- **Stage and headline:** only the asking, ratifying and review stages become queued, which matches how an issue already shows once its comment is read. The headline isn't recalculated, and it catches up on the next refresh.
- **Leftover "Posted" line:** on /act, a card forgets its own "Posted" note once the snapshot shows the issue acted on. If the issue waits again later, its card offers the actions again; before, it showed "Posted" for as long as the tab was open.

**For whoever merges**
- `act.go` is in the trusted base, so a person has to merge this.
- No decision records this yet. Whoever merges it should record one that refines D-0093.
